h: Oxford Gems to Pair With Your Round
p: A quick note on groups: smaller teams keep things moving and mean less standing about between shots. That's perfect for a bit of rivalry, so pick your teams before you arrive and have a forfeit ready for the losers. Arrive a few minutes early to get drinks sorted before your tee time.

Oxford is a compact city, so it's easy to see a lot on foot. The Bodleian Library is one of the most famous libraries in the world, and guided tours let you peek inside some of its historic rooms. Climb Carfax Tower for views over the city's rooftops and spires, or visit the Oxford University Museum of Natural History, with its soaring glass roof, dinosaur skeletons and a famous dodo. The Pitt Rivers Museum is tucked away behind it and is packed with curious objects.

If you want a breather, the University of Oxford Botanic Garden by Magdalen Bridge is a peaceful oasis, and in warmer months you can watch the punts drifting by on the Cherwell. Port Meadow is a huge open space to the north-west of the city centre, perfect for a long walk with views back to the spires.
For a bigger day out, Blenheim Palace at Woodstock is just a short drive north of Oxford. The birthplace of Winston Churchill, it has grand rooms, vast parkland and gardens to explore.
